newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firmer late, interbank steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firmer late, interbank steady.

text.p: A second consecutive day of central bank intervention in the spot market brought the baht back from record lows against the dollar to close stronger on Thursday, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 31.950/32.020 per dollar on Thursday evening against an historic low of 32.550/32.770 in the morning.

The dollar was well bid throughout the day as commercial demand for the greenback again conspired to drive the baht lower until the Bank of Thailand stepped in at around the 32.60-32.70 level, dealers said.
"It was a very volatile day. The central bank has been in the market and appears to have been quite successful," said a dealer at a large local bank.
"There is still a lot of corporate demand for dollars, either to pay foreign debt or to pay for things like crude oil where big companies need $10-20 million," he said.
Trading volumes were still small, dealers said.
The baht's soft tone was likely to continue on Friday but central bank intervention was expected if the currency again pushed new lows, dealers said.
Liquidity in the overnight interbank market was steady and continued to follow the central bank's repurchase rate, dealers said.
Overnight interbank financing was offered at 15-18 percent, unchanged from the morning, dealers said.
